decisions.reason: Audio and web conferencing sits close to the core voice offer and costs little to carry, but it is commoditised and outside the firm's infrastructure direction, so it is a modest option worth holding a bit longer while demand is still unclear.
The metro data centre connection network has documented adoption by data centres and financial hubs, so the option is resolving favourably and fits the firm's infrastructure strategy.
Optical spectrum connectivity uses the owned fibre assets, gets a dedicated page, and matches the high-bandwidth strategy, so its upside remains open at low carrying cost.
A voice number ordering portal is a cheap software layer that supports real-time provisioning, so keeping it costs little.
Carrier pre-selection telephony is a declining legacy service whose value is unlikely to grow, but the cost of carrying it is low, so it stays for now under real risk of being dropped.
Direct voice network connection is core to the enterprise voice and SIP transition, with low incremental cost and continuing demand.
